title: Everclear Hangover: Why It Hits So Hard and How to Recover
excerpt: Why Everclear and high-proof grain alcohol cause such bad hangovers, how much alcohol is really in a shot, how to recover, and how moonshine and methanol differ.
metaDescription: Why Everclear hangovers are so bad, how many drinks are really in a shot, how to recover, and how to tell a moonshine hangover from methanol poisoning.
author: DHM Guide Team
content:
**Safety first:** 190-proof Everclear is 95% alcohol, and a single straight shot holds about as much alcohol as two or three regular shots. That makes alcohol poisoning a real risk, not just a bad morning. If someone can't be woken, is breathing slowly or irregularly, is vomiting while confused, or has cold, bluish skin, call 911 and see our guide to [the signs of alcohol poisoning](/never-hungover/alcohol-poisoning-signs).

**The honest answer on the hangover:** an Everclear hangover is usually brutal for one simple reason. Everclear is so strong that people drink far more alcohol than they think. The 190-proof version is 95% alcohol, more than twice the strength of regular vodka, and it's most often poured into sweet punches where you can't taste how much is in each cup. Everclear itself is a clean, neutral spirit without many of the impurities linked to worse hangovers. So the hangover isn't caused by something special in the bottle. It's caused by the dose.

That also covers most of what people search for under "moonshine hangover", with one important difference: legal, store-bought moonshine behaves like any other spirit, but homemade or unlabeled liquor can contain methanol, and methanol poisoning can look like a bad hangover at first. This guide explains why Everclear hits so hard, how to recover the morning after, how to tell a hangover from something more serious, and how to drink high-proof alcohol (if you choose to) without wrecking the next day.

> **When to see a doctor or call 911.** A hangover is miserable but it passes. Get help right away if someone who has been drinking is confused or can't be woken, is breathing slowly or irregularly (fewer than about 8 breaths a minute or long gaps between breaths), has a seizure, has pale, bluish, or cold skin, or keeps vomiting while drowsy. Those are signs of alcohol poisoning. Also get emergency care if, 12 to 24 hours after drinking homemade, unlabeled, or suspicious liquor, someone develops blurred or "snowy" vision, severe stomach pain, or trouble breathing. That pattern can mean methanol poisoning, which needs fast treatment. Call 911 in an emergency, or Poison Control at **1-800-222-1222** (US) for advice. This article is general information, not medical advice.

## What Everclear Actually Is

Everclear is a brand of rectified grain spirit. "Rectified" means it has been distilled over and over until almost everything except ethanol and water is stripped out. The result has very little smell or flavor, which is why it's used for infusions, homemade liqueurs like limoncello, tinctures, baking extracts, and, at parties, for punches that are much stronger than they taste.

It comes in a few strengths depending on where you live:

| Version | Alcohol by volume | How it compares to regular vodka (40%) |
|---|---|---|
| 190 proof | 95% | About 2.4 times as strong |
| 151 proof | 75.5% | About 1.9 times as strong |
| 120 proof (sold in some areas) | 60% | About 1.5 times as strong |

Several US states restrict or ban the sale of 190-proof grain alcohol, which is why the 151-proof version exists. The bottle itself warns that the product is flammable and is meant to be mixed rather than drunk straight. Those warnings are worth taking literally.

## Why Everclear Hangovers Hit So Hard

### 1. The dose is much bigger than it looks

A standard drink in the US contains about 14 grams of pure alcohol. That's roughly a 12-ounce beer, a 5-ounce glass of wine, or a 1.5-ounce shot of 80-proof liquor. Everclear breaks that math:

- **One 1.5-ounce shot of 190-proof Everclear is about 2.4 standard drinks.**
- **One 1.5-ounce shot of 151-proof Everclear is about 1.9 standard drinks.**
- **A single standard drink of 190-proof Everclear is only about 0.6 ounces**, less than half a normal shot.

So if someone has "four shots" of 190-proof, their body is dealing with roughly the same alcohol as nine or ten regular shots. Most people would never knowingly drink ten shots in an evening. With Everclear they can do it without realizing.

### 2. It's usually hidden in punch

Everclear's most common party use is in jungle juice, borg drinks, and other big-batch punches. These are mixed with juice, soda, sports drinks, or flavored powders, which mask the burn completely. The person making the batch rarely measures carefully, and the person drinking it has no idea whether a cup holds one standard drink or four. Sugar and fruit flavor also make it easy to drink fast. Our guide to [the borg drink](/never-hungover/borg-drink) covers why personal, measured containers are safer than a shared bucket.

### 3. Your body feels it late

Alcohol takes time to be absorbed, often 30 to 90 minutes to reach its peak in the blood, longer with food. When you drink very concentrated alcohol quickly, you can keep drinking through that delay and find yourself far drunker an hour later than you felt when you poured your last cup. That lag is why high-proof alcohol is behind so many blackouts and emergency room visits on college campuses. See our page on [blacking out](/never-hungover/blackout-drunk) for what happens in the brain when memory switches off.

### 4. Strong spirits are rough on the stomach

Very concentrated alcohol irritates the lining of the throat, esophagus, and stomach. Even mixed, a strong punch delivers a lot of alcohol to the stomach at once. That contributes to the nausea, burning, and vomiting many people report after an Everclear night. If you're throwing up yellow or green fluid the next morning, our page on [throwing up bile after drinking](/never-hungover/throwing-up-bile-after-drinking) explains what that means and when it's a concern.

### 5. The usual hangover causes, turned up

Everything that causes an ordinary hangover gets bigger with a bigger dose:

- **Dehydration.** Alcohol blocks a hormone (vasopressin) that tells your kidneys to hold onto water, so you lose more fluid than you drink. More alcohol means more fluid loss. Our guide on [whether alcohol dehydrates you](/never-hungover/does-alcohol-dehydrate-you) explains how much of a hangover is really dehydration (less than people think, but it matters).
- **Acetaldehyde.** Your liver breaks alcohol into acetaldehyde, a toxic compound, before turning it into harmless acetate. A big load of alcohol can produce more acetaldehyde than your body clears quickly.
- **Poor sleep.** Alcohol may help you fall asleep, but it disrupts deep sleep and REM sleep in the second half of the night. Heavy drinking means more disrupted sleep.
- **Inflammation and low blood sugar.** Heavy drinking triggers an inflammatory response and can lower blood sugar, which adds to fatigue, shakiness, and brain fog.

## Is Everclear Worse Than Vodka? The Congener Question

People often assume Everclear must cause a "dirtier" hangover than other spirits. The opposite is closer to the truth, drink for drink.

**Congeners** are the by-products of fermentation and aging that give dark spirits like bourbon, brandy, and red wine their flavor. Some research has linked them to worse hangovers. In a well-known study published in *Alcoholism: Clinical and Experimental Research* in 2010, researchers led by Damaris Rohsenow gave volunteers either bourbon or vodka to the same breath alcohol level, and the bourbon group reported somewhat worse hangovers the next morning. The difference was real but modest. The amount of alcohol mattered much more than the type.

Everclear, like vodka, is highly purified and very low in congeners. So if you could drink Everclear diluted to vodka strength, in the same number of standard drinks, you'd expect a hangover much like a vodka hangover. Our article on [congeners in alcohol](/never-hungover/congeners-in-alcohol) and our guide to the [best vodka for avoiding a hangover](/never-hungover/best-vodka-for-no-hangover) go deeper on this.

The catch is that nobody drinks Everclear in neat, measured standard drinks. The low congener content is completely overwhelmed by the huge alcohol content. Clean spirit, big dose, bad morning.

## Moonshine Hangovers: What's the Same and What's Different

"Moonshine" now means two very different things, and the difference matters for your safety.

### Legal moonshine from a store

Many brands sold in liquor stores call themselves moonshine. These are commercially distilled, legally regulated spirits, usually unaged corn whiskey or flavored versions of it. They're tested and labeled like any other liquor. A hangover from legal moonshine works the same way as any spirit hangover:

- **Strength matters most.** Many moonshines are 80 to 100 proof, and some are stronger. Check the label and count standard drinks the same way you would for Everclear.
- **Congeners may be a little higher** than vodka, since unaged corn spirits keep more flavor compounds than heavily rectified grain alcohol. That might make the hangover slightly worse drink for drink, but again, the amount matters far more.
- **Flavored versions (apple pie, peach, cherry) are sweet and easy to drink**, which leads to the same pacing problem as Everclear punch.

### Homemade or illegal moonshine: the methanol boundary

Homemade and black-market spirits aren't tested by anyone. Two contaminants are worth knowing about:

- **Methanol.** All fermentation makes a small amount of methanol, and a careful distiller removes the first part of the run (the "heads") where it concentrates. Sloppy distilling can leave too much in. A larger and more common danger worldwide is liquor that's been deliberately cut with cheap industrial methanol, which has caused mass poisonings in many countries, including tourist areas.
- **Lead and other metals.** Stills improvised from old car radiators or soldered parts have historically contaminated moonshine with lead.

**Methanol poisoning is not a hangover, even though it can start out looking like one.** Here's why it's tricky: your body breaks down methanol using the same enzyme it uses for regular alcohol. While ethanol is in your system, it occupies that enzyme, which slows the methanol down. Once the regular alcohol is cleared, the methanol gets processed into formic acid, which damages the optic nerve and makes the blood acidic. That's why symptoms often show up 12 to 24 hours after drinking, right when you'd expect to be recovering.

Warning signs that point to methanol rather than a hangover:

- Blurred vision, seeing spots or a "snowstorm" effect, or vision loss
- Severe abdominal pain
- Fast or labored breathing
- Getting worse the day after drinking instead of better
- Several people who drank the same liquor feeling unusually sick

If any of this happens after drinking homemade, unlabeled, or suspiciously cheap liquor, go to an emergency room or call 911. Hospitals have an antidote (fomepizole) and other treatments, and speed protects eyesight and life. Don't wait it out.

The simple rule: **if you didn't buy it sealed from a licensed store or bar, don't drink it.** That goes double when traveling.

## How to Recover From an Everclear Hangover

There is no cure for a hangover, only ways to feel less awful while your body finishes the job. These are the steps with the most sense behind them.

### First, make sure it's only a hangover

Before you treat it as a hangover, check that you or your friend isn't still dangerously drunk. If someone is very hard to wake, confused, vomiting while barely conscious, or breathing slowly, that's an emergency. Our guide to [the signs of alcohol poisoning](/never-hungover/alcohol-poisoning-signs) walks through what to look for. After a heavy Everclear night, it's also worth remembering that you may still be over the legal limit the next morning, so don't drive until you're sure you've cleared the alcohol.

### Rehydrate, slowly

Sip water steadily rather than chugging a big glass, which can trigger vomiting on an upset stomach. An oral rehydration drink or a sports drink can help replace lost sodium and potassium, especially if you've been sick. If you can't keep any fluids down for several hours, that's a reason to see a doctor, since you may need IV fluids.

### Eat something bland

Toast, crackers, bananas, rice, eggs, or broth are easy on the stomach and help bring your blood sugar back up. Small amounts often go down better than a big meal. Greasy food the morning after doesn't "soak up" alcohol that's already in your blood, but if a breakfast sandwich is what you can stomach, it's fine.

### Pick a painkiller carefully

- **Ibuprofen or naproxen** can help a headache but irritate the stomach. Take with food, and skip them if your stomach is already burning or you've been vomiting.
- **Acetaminophen (Tylenol)** is easier on the stomach but harder on the liver after heavy drinking. Our guide on [Tylenol and alcohol](/never-hungover/tylenol-and-alcohol) explains when it's reasonable and when to avoid it.
- **Don't take any painkiller "pre-emptively" before bed** after a heavy night.

### Rest, and skip the hair of the dog

Sleep is the single best repair tool you have. Drinking more alcohol in the morning only delays the hangover and adds to the total your body has to clear. Our guide on [whether hair of the dog works](/never-hungover/does-hair-of-the-dog-work) explains why it feels like it helps briefly.

### What about anxiety, shakes, and a racing heart?

Heavy nights often leave people jittery, anxious, or shaky the next day. In a social drinker, this usually reflects the nervous system rebounding after a big dose of a sedative, plus poor sleep and low blood sugar, and it fades over the day. If you get the shakes regularly, need a drink to feel steady, or have shaking with confusion, fever, or hallucinations, that's a sign of alcohol withdrawal and you should talk to a doctor. See our page on [hangover shakes](/never-hungover/hangover-shakes) for the difference.

## How Long Does an Everclear Hangover Last?

Most hangovers peak when your blood alcohol returns to around zero and ease within about 24 hours. After a lot of high-proof alcohol, two things stretch the timeline:

1. **You may still be clearing alcohol in the morning.** The body processes roughly one standard drink per hour, though that varies from person to person. If you drank the equivalent of 12 standard drinks, which is only five shots of 190-proof Everclear, you could still have alcohol in your system well into the next day.
2. **A rough stomach slows recovery.** If you can't eat or drink, rehydration and blood sugar take longer to recover.

If you're still getting worse instead of better after about a day, can't keep fluids down, or have any of the vision or breathing symptoms above, see a doctor.

## If High-Proof Alcohol Is Around: Harm-Reduction Basics

The most effective advice is the plainest: if you want to avoid an Everclear hangover, use Everclear for infusions and extracts, not for drinking games. If you're going to drink it anyway, these habits make a real difference.

- **Measure, and convert to standard drinks.** Use a jigger. Remember that about 0.6 ounces of 190-proof equals one standard drink. Decide your limit in standard drinks before the night starts.
- **Dilute it heavily.** Everclear should never be drunk straight. Mixed drinks made with a measured amount are far safer than shots or free-poured punch.
- **Be wary of shared punch.** If you don't know how much Everclear went into the bowl, assume each cup is stronger than you think. Have one, wait an hour, and see how you feel.
- **Eat a real meal first.** Food in your stomach slows alcohol absorption and softens the peak.
- **Alternate with water.** One glass of water between drinks slows your pace and helps with fluid loss.
- **Pace yourself to about one standard drink an hour.** Our guide on [how to not get drunk](/never-hungover/how-to-not-get-drunk) has practical ways to slow down at a party without being obvious about it.
- **Keep it away from flames.** High-proof alcohol catches fire easily and burns with an almost invisible flame. Flaming shots and drinking near candles, grills, or bonfires have caused serious burns.
- **Look out for friends.** Agree on a buddy system and know the signs of alcohol poisoning before you need them.

For a broader look at the habits with the best evidence behind them, see our guide on [how to prevent a hangover](/never-hungover/how-to-prevent-a-hangover).

## Where Supplements Fit (Honestly)

No supplement makes drinking high-proof alcohol safe, and none can offset ten standard drinks' worth of punch. Pacing, water, food, and simply drinking less matter far more than anything you can buy.

That said, some people add a supplement as one part of a routine for a planned night out. The most discussed is **DHM (dihydromyricetin)**, a compound from the Japanese raisin tree. Most of the research comes from animal and lab studies on how it affects alcohol metabolism and the liver, with only limited human data. There is no good evidence that it prevents or cures hangovers in people, and it won't protect you from alcohol poisoning or methanol. If you want to try it alongside sensible drinking, popular options include [No Days Wasted DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) and the lower-cost [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20). Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) covers timing and amounts, and our [supplement reviews](/reviews) compare brands.

## The Bottom Line

- An Everclear hangover is mostly a dose problem. A shot of 190-proof is about 2.4 standard drinks, and punch hides how much you're drinking.
- Drink for drink, Everclear is a clean, low-congener spirit like vodka. The amount, not impurities, is what makes the morning so bad.
- Legal moonshine works like any other spirit. Homemade or unlabeled liquor can contain methanol, and blurred vision, severe stomach pain, or getting worse 12 to 24 hours later means emergency care, not hangover care.
- To recover: confirm it's only a hangover, rehydrate slowly, eat something bland, choose a painkiller carefully, rest, and skip more alcohol.
- To avoid it next time: measure, dilute, pace to about one standard drink an hour, eat first, and treat shared punch with suspicion.

If the proof numbers are confusing, our explainer on [what proof means](/never-hungover/what-does-proof-mean) walks through how proof converts to alcohol percentage and standard drinks.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Why are Everclear hangovers so bad?**

Mostly because of dose. A 1.5-ounce shot of 190-proof Everclear holds about as much alcohol as two and a third regular shots of 80-proof vodka, and it's often hidden in sweet punches where nobody can tell how strong each cup is. More alcohol means more dehydration, worse sleep, more stomach irritation, and more acetaldehyde, the toxic by-product your liver makes while breaking alcohol down. Everclear itself is a clean, neutral spirit, so the problem is the amount, not some extra impurity.

**Is an Everclear hangover worse than a vodka hangover?**

Drink for drink, not really. Both are neutral grain spirits with very few congeners (the flavor by-products linked to worse hangovers in darker drinks). The difference is that a 'drink' of Everclear contains far more alcohol than a drink of vodka, so people end up taking in much more than they realize. If you diluted Everclear down to vodka strength and drank the same number of standard drinks, you'd expect a similar hangover.

**How many shots of Everclear equal a regular shot?**

One 1.5-ounce shot of 190-proof (95% alcohol) Everclear equals roughly 2.4 standard US drinks, or about two and a third regular 80-proof shots. One 1.5-ounce shot of the 151-proof version (75.5% alcohol) equals roughly 1.9 standard drinks. Put differently, a standard drink's worth of 190-proof Everclear is only about 0.6 ounces.

**Is a moonshine hangover different from a regular hangover?**

Legal moonshine sold in liquor stores is a regulated commercial spirit, so its hangover works like any other spirit's: strength and amount matter most, and unaged corn whiskey may carry a few more congeners than vodka. Illegally made or homemade spirits are different because nobody checks them for methanol or other contaminants. If someone feels much worse 12 to 24 hours after drinking homemade or unlabeled liquor, especially with blurred vision or severe stomach pain, that is not a hangover and needs emergency care.

**How long does an Everclear hangover last?**

Most hangovers ease within about 24 hours, and the worst of it usually passes by the afternoon or evening after drinking. A night with a lot of high-proof alcohol can stretch that, partly because your body may still be clearing alcohol well into the next morning. If symptoms are getting worse instead of better after a day, or you can't keep fluids down, check in with a doctor.

**Can you die from drinking Everclear?**

Yes, if you drink enough of it quickly. Everclear isn't uniquely poisonous, but its strength makes it easy to reach a dangerous blood alcohol level before you feel the full effect. Signs of alcohol poisoning include confusion, repeated vomiting, seizures, slow or irregular breathing, pale or bluish skin, low body temperature, and being hard to wake. If you see any of these, call 911 and don't leave the person alone.

**Does DHM help with an Everclear hangover?**

There is no good evidence that DHM prevents or cures a hangover from high-proof alcohol, and nothing makes drinking straight grain alcohol safe. DHM is a plant compound studied mostly in animals and lab work for its effects on alcohol metabolism, with limited human data. Some people take it as part of a routine alongside water, food, and pacing, but the biggest lever with Everclear is simply drinking less of it.
